observations.hierarchy: The broad-winged animal dominates the canvas. The separate fire and two small crossed logs are a much smaller lower-left accent, rather than an equal second subject.
observations.poseAndEyes: Four broad pale wings fan around the compact bronze body. The golden terminal abdomen trails down-right. Two dark faceted eyes are visible on the front three-quarter head, with the far eye naturally narrower.
observations.drawingAndMaterial: Connected flat bronze, copper, champagne, and honey-gold facets cover the head, body, abdomen, and wings. Cool gray-violet facets accent some wing shadows. The little flame has organic curved tongues and continuous warm shading; the crossed wood has restrained physical grain.
observations.interestPoint: A small separate foreground flame with two crossed wood pieces sits below and left of the animal.
observations.matteAndEffects: Near-white rather than uniform pure-white matte, solid pale wing planes, and no obvious external glow. Edge extraction has not been tested.
caveats: The wing tips come closer to the canvas edges than the planned safe margins.
A visible gap separates the flame from the lower wing; the intended narrow foreground overlap is absent.
The legs retain angular articulated shapes and the head has pronounced eye facets.
The animal is broader than the planned combined bounds; round-corner clearance needs review after raw approval.
